notes: Extracted 29 October 2026 from the guide (src/guides/chipselect.guide.tsx, self-contained) and docs/evidence/chipselect.md at 4e470cf (“docs: adopt Biscuit's main at 3795b4c (v0.1.78-3795b4c)”, 2 October), the same files on main and docs-next (no diff from 4e470cf to docs-next 7d6f6d0 or main 662c2ad); 4e470cf changed only the Sources date, 28 September to 1 October. The evidence has a 28 September check on 0.1.60 (Sources, Contract, Rendered, Limits, Verification) and a “0.1.78 check” on 1 October against mirror tag v0.1.78 (Biscuit's fix/component-bugs-v0.1.78 at 5b6894b) in headless Chrome with react-native-web 0.21.2; the guide's Sources note says “Checked 1 October 2026” on 0.1.78, so items citing it, and the 0.1.78 check, carry 2026-10-01 and 0.1.78-5b6894b (the same version as installed, so the trace check does not flag them); the one item citing the 28 September Contract carries 2026-09-28 and 0.1.60 and is flagged. Installed build: jfs-components 0.1.78, mirror v0.1.78-dbe0e02 (Biscuit's main at dbe0e02, 27 October), react-native-web 0.21.2. Builds compared through gh api: ChipSelect.tsx is the same blob (654d98d) at v0.1.78, -3795b4c, -636f3f5, -c1fa197, -a116616, -c7d3348 and -dbe0e02; its last change is b9652a2 (1 October, the 0.1.78 build). The design-tokens JSON is 0582bb0 at v0.1.78 and 4545aec at dbe0e02, with the same resolver, and every chipSelect/* token resolves to the same value on both through the package's own getVariableByName (no modes, ChipSelect State Idle and Active, and Color Mode Dark): gap 4, padding 0 vertical and 16 horizontal, radius 999, label 14 px on a 32 px line, weight 700, JioType Var, icon 16; Idle background rgb(245, 245, 245) and foreground rgb(13, 13, 15); Active background rgb(246, 243, 255) and foreground rgb(93, 0, 181). Icon.tsx changed only in its loading Skeleton (visible={loading === true}), which ChipSelect doesn't use. Every guide sentence quoted here was read against the installed ChipSelect.tsx (read, not rendered): active sets ChipSelect State itself after any modes passed in (84–89), so a passed ChipSelect State is overridden (the 0.1.60 Contract sentence still holds); the pill is chipSelect/radius 999 with no vertical padding and no width, so it is 32 px high (the label's line height, 104 and 126) and hugs the leading icon, label and close icon (111–129); the label and icons take chipSelect/foreground, on chipSelect/background (98–101, 139, 160, 166), grey and dark when Idle, lavender and purple when Active, as the States cards say (in Light); the leading icon is drawn whenever icon is set, in both states (159–161), default ic_calendar_week (74), so the Sources' “The leading icon shows in both states, as in Figma.” holds and the JSDoc's “Icon name to display in Idle state (when active is false).” (28, and the generated fact's description) does not: the evidence fact on icon carries the Sources sentence; the close icon is ic_close, drawn only when active and showCloseIcon (165–167; showCloseIcon defaults to true, 75), inside the one TouchableOpacity (145–168), so the whole chip is a single press target; there is no disabled prop (16–65) and no internal state, so the screen owns active, label and onPress, as In context says. Web: role button (149), name accessibilityLabel ?? label (142, 150), accessibilityHint (151), accessibilityState selected (152) and aria-pressed = active (154–156); react-native-web 0.21.2 renders role button as a button element (dist/modules/AccessibilityUtil/propsToAccessibilityComponent.js 15) and presses it on Enter and Space (dist/modules/usePressEvents/PressResponder.js 66–71), so the Sources' “Enter and click activate it” holds (Space works too; the guide doesn't claim it). ic_calendar_week, ic_filter, ic_close and ic_home are in the installed icon registry (src/icons/registry.ts; ic_filter at 1937). Contradicted by the installed build: nothing, so there is no human flag. Out of date in the evidence and not used: the 28 September Contract's “No `disabled`, `testID`, or accessibility props; no rest spread.” (testID, accessibilityLabel and accessibilityHint exist now), the Rendered line “DOM: `div tabindex=0` with no role, no accessible name, and no selected/pressed state.”, and the Limits' accessibility gap and “The page must not claim selection is announced.”; the evidence's own 0.1.78 check supersedes them (#169 fixed). Not recorded: labelSlot (developer-only, per the evidence; it is cloned with the resolved modes, 131–140; with a labelSlot and no label or accessibilityLabel the chip's name stays “Date”, a screen-reader name, so not counted as a gap); accessibilityHint and testID (the guide doesn't cover them); style (the building rules keep style off Coin components); Color Mode (building rules; the Dark Active colours are token ticket #201, not a Coin gap here); the pressed opacity 0.8 (evidence, 0.1.60; the guide is silent); Figma's 84 × 32 and 104 × 32 against the rendered 85.8 and 105.8 (font rasterisation, per the evidence; Sizing's specimen shows 86 × 32; not a gap); the Sources' “Declared and installed jfs-components is 0.1.78 from the team’s private package repository.” (the docs now install the mirror tag, package.json line 27; not quoted); the Storybook story list; the In context readout; the playground. Structure: useWhen is the summary; the In context title is placement, as in Chip Group's entry; avoidWhen is the States' no disabled state (hide a filter that does not apply), with no useInstead (the guide names no other component); configuration keeps the guide's In context behaviour in its context (round 1, below). Anatomy required: Leading icon false (icon && …: drawn by default, an empty icon hides it, as the evidence says); Label true; Close icon false (Active with showCloseIcon only); Container true. States are the guide's Idle and Active cards. Content good keeps the Idle and Applied labels; bad is empty (the Don't's “Date” is bad only once Active, and Date is the guide's Idle label). Strength: only “Only when a press reopens the picker instead of clearing.” holds an absolute word; it applies to every Chip Select (scope everywhere) but nothing in the package checks what a press does, so it stays recommended. Sizing: “Height is fixed at 32 px.” holds for the chip itself (no height prop; its label line is 32 px and on its own the label never wraps: the chip grows with it). Inside a ChipGroup narrower than a chip, the group gives each chip maxWidth 100%, flexShrink 1, minWidth 0 and overflow hidden (ChipGroup.tsx 20–25 and 142, since c1fa197), the label wraps and the chip grows taller; that is ChipGroup's behaviour and its entry says so (“A chip wider than the row wraps its label to stay inside it.”), so the sentence is quoted as the guide says. Read from source, not rendered: ChipSelect sets no alignSelf, so a lone chip placed straight in a VStack (cross-axis stretch by default, src/utils/stackAlignment.ts 10) stretches to the column's width; in a row (HStack, ChipGroup, the guide's CSS row) it hugs its label. The guide doesn't cover it, so it is not in the entry; reported to the coordinator. Examples follow the building rules: no Color Mode (the guide sets Light on every chip), no modes, no style. The first is the guide's In context once the date filter is applied (its In context code toggles between “Date” and “Last 30 days”, lines 85–86); the guide lays the two chips out in a CSS row (coin-new-content-list: flex, wrap, gap 10 px), which a ChipGroup stands in for here (wrap, gap 8): Chip Group's entry is the pack's component for a row of Chip Select filters (“Use a Chip Group to lay out a row of Chip Select filters that wraps onto new lines with even gaps.”) and recommends naming the row (“Transaction filters”, its /accessibility/0), and building.md's first rule is the largest block that fits. The second is Configuration's Active without close icon; the third is one Idle attribute filter (Configuration's Filter icon card, Category with ic_filter, line 49). ChipGroup and ChipSelect have entries; icons are the guide's own (CAL and FILTER, lines 9–10). Left out of examples (three at most): the Anatomy and Sizing specimens, the States cards, the Don'ts (the generic label, the home icon, the hidden ×) and the playground. Consistency: only chipgroup.json uses ChipSelect. It agrees with this entry: a single filter is a ChipSelect alone (its /avoidWhen/2, useInstead ChipSelect) and several combinable filters go in a Chip Group; each chip owns its active and onPress and is announced as its own toggle (aria-pressed); ChipSelect State can't be set from outside (its modes evidence fact, and this entry's); an applied chip shows its value and a close icon and grows 20 px (16 px icon + 4 px gap, as read here); match each icon to its filter; one or two words while Idle; the chosen value once applied; its examples use ic_calendar_week and the chips' active and onPress the same way. The one nuance is the wrapped label above. No other entry uses ChipSelect; productoverview's “Chip” part is its own. Sorting (batch 14, two cross-check runs). Round 1 flagged /configuration/5 (generalises-example: the In context press behaviour stated as a general onPress rule, though Configuration also allows an Active chip whose press reopens the picker); our misreading, so the item now says it is the guide's In context and that the screen owns what a press does. Round 1 also flagged /examples/0 (misreads-source: ChipGroup and its “Transaction filters” name are not in this guide); round 2, on the reworded entry, did not flag it and kept it as a note for a human to confirm the cross-entry choice (the reasons are above). Round 2 flagged /configuration/11 (misreads-source: ic_filter is not in the rendered copy); dismissed in reviews/chipselect.json, since the name is the guide's own (line 10, const FILTER = 'ic_filter', used by the Filter icon card at line 49) and is in the installed registry. Round 2's notes, not flags: confirm ic_filter (done, above); the 28 September evidence lines are superseded by the 0.1.78 check, and /accessibility/0 follows the newer check. The last cross-check (round 2) ran on the entry's final form. Left: one trace-check flag, /facts/modes/0 (ChipSelect State, 0.1.60 evidence), still true on dbe0e02 (ChipSelect.tsx 84–89). No guide fix and no Component Bug proposed.

examples.purpose: Filters above a transaction list, the guide's In context, once the screen has applied the date filter: the date chip is Active and shows its value, “Last 30 days”, with the close icon (a press clears it); Category is Idle (a press opens the screen's picker, which is not part of Chip Select). The row is a ChipGroup, the pack's component for a row of Chip Select filters (the guide's own code lays the two chips out in a plain wrapping row), named “Transaction filters” as the ChipGroup entry advises. The literal values and empty onPress stand for the screen's own state and picker.
